tele-079.explication: The AF detection algorithms of implantable loop recorders rely mainly on RR irregularity: frequent PACs, sinus arrhythmia or intermittent undersensing may be wrongly classified as AF. P waves visible before each QRS rule out AF. Good practice is to review the EGMs, classify the false positives and adjust the parameters (algorithm sensitivity, minimum episode duration, ectopy filters) to reduce workload without missing true AF. Disabling all alerts would defeat the purpose of the device. Anticoagulating on the basis of false episodes would be a serious error.
tele-079.aRetenir: False AF on a loop recorder: review, classify, reprogram, without disabling everything.
tele-079.rappel: Implantable loop recorders detect AF mainly from the irregularity and incoherence of RR intervals over a time window, with some algorithms also looking for P waves. Any cause of RR irregularity can therefore produce false AF: frequent PACs or PVCs, sinus arrhythmia, intermittent undersensing or oversensing. The diagnosis relies on the reviewed EGM: P waves visible before every QRS exclude AF. Programming (algorithm sensitivity, minimum episode duration, ectopy filters) is tailored to the indication to reduce false positives without missing true AF.

tele-080.question: Implantable loop recorder inserted for recurrent unexplained syncope. Transmission: a 7-second pause with several consecutive P waves not followed by QRS complexes, coinciding with a presyncopal episode reported by the patient. What should be done?
options: Start a beta-blocker and check the next transmission in one month
Simple follow-up: wait for a documented recurrence before any decision
Contact the patient the same day and arrange pacing promptly
Arrange a tilt test to confirm a reflex mechanism
commentaires: Incorrect: a beta-blocker would worsen the conduction disorder.
Incorrect (under-reaction): symptom–rhythm correlation is already established; waiting exposes the patient to a traumatic recurrence.
Correct: symptomatic paroxysmal AV block = pacing indication; a "red" alert, with instructions to call the emergency services (15 in France).
Incorrect: a tilt test adds nothing once symptom–rhythm correlation has been documented.
tele-080.explication: Non-conducted P waves during a pause coinciding with symptoms document symptomatic paroxysmal AV block, which explains the syncope. The 2018 ESC syncope guidelines and 2021 ESC pacing guidelines give an indication for cardiac pacing in this situation. It is a critical alert (the 2023 HRS consensus classifies a pause of at least 6 seconds on an implantable loop recorder as "red"): the patient must be contacted the same day, informed of the risk and referred for prompt implantation, with instructions on what to do in case of recurrence. A tilt test is of no value once symptom–rhythm correlation has been established, and a beta-blocker would worsen the conduction disorder.
tele-080.aRetenir: Pause due to AV block correlated with symptoms on a loop recorder = pacing, same-day contact.
tele-080.rappel: An implantable loop recorder is indicated for recurrent unexplained syncope, particularly when an arrhythmic cause is suspected, once the initial work-up has been inconclusive. Its main value is symptom–rhythm correlation: syncope or presyncope coinciding with significant bradycardia (AV block, pause) establishes the diagnosis and points to pacing. Paroxysmal AV block is recognised by P waves not followed by QRS complexes during the pause, whereas a sinus pause shows an isoelectric line with no P waves. Rate-slowing drugs should be avoided while awaiting pacing.

tele-081.question: True or false: a large proportion of alerts transmitted by implantable loop recorders are false detections, which justifies systematic EGM review and optimisation of programming.
options: True
False
commentaires: Correct: false pauses, false tachycardias and false AF are common; every decision is based on the reviewed EGM.
Incorrect: the proportion of false positives is substantial, as the 2023 HRS consensus highlights.
tele-081.explication: Implantable loop recorders generate a substantial proportion of false positives: false pauses from undersensing, false tachycardias from oversensing of noise, myopotentials or T waves, and false AF from PACs or sinus arrhythmia. The 2023 HRS consensus highlights the resulting workload for clinics and recommends programming tailored to the indication, EGM review and false-positive reduction algorithms. No decision (pacemaker, anticoagulant) should rest on an unverified automatic classification.
tele-081.aRetenir: Implantable loop recorder: many false positives, always review the EGM.
tele-081.rappel: Implantable loop recorders generate a large proportion of false positives, because of a low-amplitude subcutaneous signal and algorithms based mainly on RR intervals. The three main families are false pauses (QRS undersensing), false tachycardias (oversensing of noise, myopotentials, large T or P waves) and false AF (PACs, sinus arrhythmia). This creates a heavy workload for clinics. An automatic classification is never a diagnosis: every transmitted episode must be reviewed before any treatment decision.

tele-082.question: A clinic receives dozens of irrelevant alerts a month from the same implantable loop recorder. What measures do you propose to reduce this burden without compromising safety?
tele-082.reponseAttendue: Review the EGMs to identify the type of false positive (undersensing, noise, PACs, T waves). Tailor programming to the indication (disable unnecessary detections, e.g. AF if the indication is syncope and AF is not the goal; adjust pause and tachycardia thresholds, sensitivity and minimum duration). Enable the available false-positive reduction algorithms. Define in the protocol which alerts are transmitted as a priority. Reassess the indication and consider explantation once the goal has been achieved or the battery is depleted.
tele-082.explication: The 2023 HRS consensus identifies alert overload as a major problem in remote monitoring, particularly for implantable loop recorders. Programming should be individualised according to the indication (syncope, AF detection after stroke, palpitations) and revised after analysis of false positives. Manufacturers offer filters and algorithms to reduce false detections, which should be enabled and evaluated. Safety is preserved if the alerts relevant to the indication are kept and transmitted episodes continue to be reviewed. The pitfall is to disable all alerts to "relieve" the team.
tele-082.aRetenir: Reducing false alerts = programming tailored to the indication, filters and targeted review, never blanket deactivation.
tele-082.rappel: Implantable loop recorder programming must match the indication: syncope (detection of pauses and bradycardia, patient-activated recording), AF detection after cryptogenic stroke (AF algorithm, minimum episode duration), palpitations (tachycardias). Detections unrelated to the clinical question can be switched off or made less sensitive, and false-positive reduction filters and algorithms enabled. Programming is revised on the basis of an analysis of the false positives observed. Once the diagnostic goal is reached or the battery is depleted, explantation is considered.

tele-083.question: Which situations can cause false detections on an implantable loop recorder?
options: Reduced QRS amplitude, causing false pauses
Myopotentials or noise, causing false tachycardias
Frequent premature atrial contractions, causing false AF
Sinus pause during a vasovagal episode
Paroxysmal AV block with non-conducted P waves
commentaires: Correct: the QRS complexes fall below the sensing threshold and the device wrongly concludes that there is a pause.
Correct: oversensing of noise or myopotentials creates false tachycardias.
Correct: RR irregularity due to PACs is wrongly classified as AF.
Incorrect: a vagal sinus pause is a true event, not a false detection.
Incorrect: this is a true diagnosis, which may warrant a pacemaker.
tele-083.explication: The implantable loop recorder records a low-amplitude subcutaneous signal between two closely spaced electrodes. Undersensing of QRS complexes produces false pauses, oversensing (noise, myopotentials, large T or P waves) produces false tachycardias, and RR irregularity due to PACs or sinus arrhythmia produces false AF. Vagal sinus pause and paroxysmal AV block are not false detections: they are true diagnoses, recognisable by an isoelectric line (with P waves not followed by QRS complexes in AV block), which may explain syncope. Hence the need to review every EGM before drawing conclusions.
tele-083.aRetenir: Implantable loop recorder: undersensing = false pauses; oversensing and PACs = false tachycardias and false AF.
tele-083.rappel: The signal of an implantable loop recorder is a closely spaced bipolar subcutaneous ECG, of low amplitude that varies with device position, posture and movement. False detections follow three mechanisms: undersensing (QRS complexes too small, causing false pauses or false bradycardia), oversensing (myopotentials, contact noise, large T or P waves, causing false tachycardias) and misclassification (RR irregularity without AF, causing false AF). Conversely, sinus pauses and paroxysmal AV block are true events that can explain syncope.

tele-084.question: Which of the following alerts cannot apply to a leadless pacemaker (ventricular capsule type)?
options: Rise in pacing threshold
Fracture or insulation breach
Premature battery depletion
R-wave sensing abnormality
commentaires: Incorrect: the threshold can rise, as with a conventional lead.
Correct: with no transvenous lead, there can be no conductor fracture or insulation breach.
Incorrect: the battery depletes and must be monitored.
Incorrect: sensing abnormalities remain possible.
tele-084.explication: Leadless pacemakers are implanted directly in the right ventricle: they eliminate complications related to transvenous leads (fracture, insulation breach, pocket infection) and to the subcutaneous generator. They remain exposed, however, to threshold rise, sensing abnormalities, battery depletion and, especially in the first few days, device dislodgement. In the Micra study, the major complication rate was lower than in a historical cohort of conventional pacemakers. Remote monitoring and device checks therefore remain fully relevant.
tele-084.aRetenir: Leadless = no fracture or insulation breach, but threshold, sensing and battery still need monitoring.
tele-084.rappel: A leadless pacemaker is a self-contained capsule implanted via the femoral vein into the right ventricle, combining generator and electrode. It eliminates complications related to the pocket and transvenous leads (fracture, insulation breach, pocket infection, pneumothorax) but has its own complications: pericardial effusion or tamponade at implantation, femoral access-site complications and device dislodgement. Its parameters must be monitored like those of a conventional pacemaker: pacing threshold, R-wave amplitude, impedance and battery.

tele-085.question: A patient with a leadless pacemaker implanted 5 days ago. The data show a pacing threshold that has risen from 0.5 V to over 3 V, with collapsed R-wave sensing. What do you fear?
options: Early battery ERI: plan device replacement
Device dislodgement or embolisation: immediate check
Transient electromagnetic interference: repeat transmission
Normal interface maturation: recheck at one month
commentaires: Incorrect: a new battery is not at ERI after 5 days.
Correct: simultaneous deterioration of threshold and sensing just after implantation = dislodgement until proven otherwise.
Incorrect (under-reaction): interference does not explain sustained deterioration of both parameters.
Incorrect (under-reaction): maturation does not cause such a collapse in sensing.
tele-085.explication: An abrupt, simultaneous deterioration of threshold and sensing in the first few days should raise suspicion of device dislodgement, or even embolisation into the pulmonary artery, a rare but serious complication described with leadless pacemakers. The patient must be assessed urgently (ECG, chest X-ray or echocardiography to locate the device) and, if it has dislodged, percutaneous retrieval and re-implantation are required. Maturation does not cause such a collapse in sensing. A new battery is not at ERI after 5 days.
tele-085.aRetenir: Threshold and sensing collapsing just after leadless pacemaker implantation = dislodgement until proven otherwise.
tele-085.rappel: A leadless pacemaker is anchored to the right ventricular endocardium by nitinol tines or a helix, depending on the model; inadequate fixation exposes the patient, especially in the first few days, to dislodgement or even embolisation into the pulmonary artery. Dislodgement causes a simultaneous deterioration in pacing threshold and R-wave amplitude, whereas an inflammatory interface reaction mainly affects the threshold. The device is located by imaging (chest X-ray, fluoroscopy, echocardiography), and management relies on percutaneous retrieval and reimplantation.
